newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - U.S. prices data sparks European share rally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. prices data sparks European share rally.

text.p: European stock markets zoomed higher on Tuesday after U.S. consumer price data was seen easing the pressure on American policy-makers to raise interest rates again.

The 0.1 percent rise in the March consumer price index (CPI) was half market expectations and sparked a rally in U.S. debt markets. The dollar rose to a fresh 37-month high against the mark, while sterling stormed to a 55-month peak against the German currency.

"It doesn't live up to investors' worst fears which is why the market is getting a nice little bounce off it," Kevin Flanagan, an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds in New York, said about the CPI figures.
European bourses, already showing moderate gains after the Dow's 60 point rise overnight, accelerated their rally as the nervously awaited figures were released.
And the Dow reopened with a bang, putting on well over one percent in the first few minutes of trade, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to impose curbs on index-arbitrage trading.

While the March CPI figure was balm to the financial markets, economists said policymakers at the U.S. Federal Reserve needed to see a slowing in consumer demand or overall economic growth before backing away from their current monetary tightening.

"I think this number does not force the Fed to have to change policy right away," said Gary Thayer, senior economist at A.G Edwards & Sons Inc in New York. "It might allow the Fed to hold policy steady if we continue to see good inflation news like this."

The market reaction to Wall Street displayed by the major European bourses was reflected amongst second-tier markets, too. Amsterdam's AEX index was showing gains of 2.7 percent by 1400 GMT, while Milan's MIBTEL was up 2.25 percent and Madrid's IBEX 35 2.4 percent.
Among the majors, the French and German bourses bounded ahead the best.

Frankfurt climbed more than two percent in post-bourse electronic trading after traders saw the Dow's early spurt. The 30-share DAX earlier ended floor trade before the CPI figures were released with a gain of 47.78 points, or 1.46 percent, to 3,327.68.
Carmaker Volkswagen fell 11 marks to 1,039 after a report showing a three percent drop in European new car registrations during March.
France's blue chip CAC 40 index was also standing nearly two percent up by 1400 GMT.
French luxury goods group LVMH rose 5.3 percent to 1,351 francs after it reported a big rise in first quarter sales.

The London stock exchange, Europe's biggest bourse, tried to join the party but failed to achieve the gains seen elsewhere. By mid-afternoon the blue chip FTSE 100 index was up 35 points, or 0.82 percent, at 4,286.7.
Some strategists doubted whether the rebound would last.

"This is a bit of a holiday in the sun for the markets, but I don't think this is a sign that the Fed is not going to tighten further," said stock strategist David Aserkoff of Credit Suisse First Boston.
"The market was geared up for a bigger rise. We don't think this rise is sustainable."
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar pushed its way up to a fresh 37-month high of 1.7350 marks with the help of strong U.S. asset markets following the CPI data.
The British pound hit a 55-month peak above 2.82 marks, boosted by strong demand from U.S. investors enticed by the unit's attractive yield.

A mixture of other factors, such as the strength of the dollar against the mark and a tough report by the European Monetary Institute on the need for better budget discipline, also added spice to sterling's rally.

"Sterling sentiment is extremely positive, and it continues to be in demand on the back of expectations that interest rate differentials will remain in favour of the UK," said James McKay, UK economist at Paine Webber.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7357 marks and 126.43 yen after ending at 1.7228 marks and 126.45 yen in late trading in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 35 points, or 0.82 percent, at 4,286.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 50.53 points, or 1.97 percent, at 2,616.66.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 47.78 points, or 1.46 percent, at 3,327.68. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX was up 68.90 points, or 2.09 percent, at 3,366.42.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $343.00 against $345.60 after support broke following New York sales. Silver was off three cents at $4.70.
